title: Myhill’s computable isomorphism theorem

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version2024-02-25; §5.2 Theorem5.7 and full finite-matching proof, p.30, with the classical comparison wording repaired; the label-preservation invariant is made explicit

summary: Build a computable permutation, with computable inverse, from two injective reductions by extending finite matchings.
abstract: Two membership problems may each translate injectively into the other while the two translations leave many inputs unused. Myhill’s theorem shows how to replace them by one computable renaming that reaches every input exactly once and preserves the membership answers. The construction repeatedly extends a finite table of pairs. An injection leads through the pairs already chosen until it reaches a fresh endpoint; alternating the two directions eventually matches every input and output. Explicit finite stages compute the resulting permutation and its inverse. The procedure never asks for the membership answers it preserves. More generally, the same table preserves any labels respected by the original injections, even when those labels are whole partial functions and cannot themselves be computed.
